toolchains.note: The host C compiler CMake already uses. C99 is the floor: the public headers use nothing newer, and the gate is what keeps it that way.
The host C++ compiler. A C ABI that a C++ consumer cannot include is only half an ABI, so every header is compiled in both languages.
GCC by name, including C23, which the host compiler may predate.
GCC's C++ driver at the standards CNA itself builds with.
A second front end catches what one compiler's extensions would hide.
Clang's C++ driver, for the same reason.
A Windows target reached by cross-compiling. Headers only: nothing here links or runs a Windows binary, and the matrix says so rather than implying a tested platform.
The matching Windows-target C++ driver. It proves the same public C headers remain consumable from Windows C++ translation units; like the C row, it compiles only.

outside_matrix.subject: Runtime and renderer behaviour
outside_matrix.note: This is a source-compatibility matrix for the public headers, not a runtime matrix. C API smoke, package, sanitizer, renderer and platform tests are registered in the applicable CMake configurations and carry their own evidence; this document does not claim that every smoke program runs under every renderer.

outside_matrix.subject: MinGW linking and execution
outside_matrix.note: The two MinGW rows cross-compile headers for a Windows target but do not link or run a Windows binary. Native Windows and Wine/DXVK runtime evidence belongs to their platform workflows, not to these header cells.

outside_matrix.subject: MSVC and Apple Clang
outside_matrix.note: Neither native compiler is a declared cell. Their platform builds and tests are useful independent evidence, but do not prove this matrix's per-header, per-language-mode contract.

outside_matrix.subject: Emscripten and Android NDK Clang
outside_matrix.note: Neither target compiler is a declared header cell. The separately built WebAssembly artifact and Android CNA builds do not imply that every public C header has been compiled alone in each language mode with those target macros and system headers.

outside_matrix.subject: C89
outside_matrix.note: The headers use `//` comments and mixed declarations, so C99 is the floor by design rather than by accident.
